fix.summary:
All ten findings are decided and the design is corrected; every one is recorded as fixed in `/Users/jmagady/dev2/vsdd-factory/rewrite/findings/outcomes/d31-fix-2.json`. The four checks are clean, nothing is left for a builder (so no `triage/d31-fix-2.json` was written), and nothing needs the user.

**D31R-C-2, the decision.** The test-writer moves an existing test that the on state breaks, by renaming it; nobody edits or drops one. The rename carries one of two tokens:
- `flag_old_<k>`: a criterion of a story behind the flag replaces everything the test asserts. It is deleted when the flag is removed.
- `flag_pending_<k>`: the test asserts behaviour the product must keep that the flag's stories do not provide yet. This is the half-finished case of clause 2b, which F-ON would otherwise have refused.

The move happens in the tests stage where the criteria show the need. Otherwise it happens after the green gate's run with the flag on names the test, through the existing `test-defects` step; no stage, step or prompt is added.

What checks that a move was honest:
- **F-STATES** requires a moved test to pass with no flag set, and refuses more missing base tests than new moved tests, so an existing test cannot simply be deleted.
- **F-ON** refuses a moved test that passes with the flag on (it gets its name back), names every other failing test, and refuses a turn-on story while a `pending` test remains.
- **F-DEFINITION** refuses a removal that leaves a test named for the off state.
- **The adversary's `flag-off` item**, which only `checked` satisfies, covers each move: an existing test, assertions unchanged, `old` only where a criterion replaces it.

I walked a feature added to existing code through red, green and review, and also a feature built over several stories, turning on, and removal. The one thing a program cannot judge is whether a test moved as `old` was really meant to go; that rests on the reviewer, and the F-ON row says so.

**The other findings.**
- **C-1:** six open D31 entries (D31-1, -2, -3, -4, -6, -8) are rewritten to match the design, with their outcome texts and triage notes. D31-5 already matched.
- **C-3:** "cannot measure" now fails only for a key F-CHOICE requires; the four keys that may be empty are named, and each has a report.
- **C-4:** F5 depends on G7.
- **C-5:** a token now ends at `__`, a non-word character or the end of the name, and the key's encoded form is defined once.
- **C-6:** "every gate result" is dropped; the line is printed by status, the briefing and the release packet.
- **C-7:** `flags.enabled` is a proposal key a person may override.
- **F-10:** each fact has one home; I removed four further restatements of the same kind beyond the three named.
- **F-19 / D-25:** the overlay is `story-behind-flag`.

**Two things for the orchestrating session**, both outside what this task may edit:
1. Step 5 of `rewrite/spec/packaging/build-plan.md` still sums F5 up as extending "the planning gates"; it should add the sweep job.
2. `vsdd env start` turns every live temporary flag on for wave and release evaluation. That includes a flag whose feature is unfinished, so hidden scenarios of existing behaviour could fail there. I did not change it; it deserves its own finding.
decisions_made: An existing test that the on state breaks is moved by the test-writer by renaming it; it is never edited, weakened or deleted, and it sets no flag.

A moved test carries `flag_old_<k>` when a criterion of a story behind the flag replaces everything it asserts, and `flag_pending_<k>` when it asserts behaviour the product must keep that the flag's stories do not provide yet.
A move is made in the tests stage where the criteria show the need, or through the existing test-defects step after F-ON names the test; no stage, step or prompt is added.
F-ON refuses a moved test that passes with the flag on, so a test the flag no longer breaks gets its own name back and runs in both states again.
A turn-on story is refused while the flag still has a `pending` test, which keeps an unfinished feature from being turned on in the repository's definitions.
A story behind a flag, or one that turns a flag on, is refused when more base tests are missing than new moved tests exist, so an existing test leaves the suite only by a move.
A moved test is not held among the story's frozen tests, so a re-freeze can undo a move made earlier in the same story.
The `flag-off` review item is also added to every turn-on story, and returns in a later review loop whose commits touch tests as well as source.

A removal story is refused while a test is still named `off`, `default` or moved for the flag; the test-writer's duty now covers a removal that keeps the off behaviour as well as one that keeps the on behaviour.
A token ends at `__`, a non-word character or the end of the name; the key's encoded form collapses runs of other characters to one `_` and is defined once, in the header of flag-checks.toml.
A story may not ship behind a flag whose encoded form another record shares.
Four keys may be empty (key_env, key_patterns, definition_patterns, definitions_check); each has a report the gate prints, and the adversary checks an empty one against the decision record.
'flags requested, flag system not chosen' is printed by vsdd status, the briefing and the release packet, and not by gate results.
flags.enabled is a proposal key that a person may override; flags.require is the only key a proposal may not carry.
What [flags.approved] holds is stated only in F-FILL; the handling of the key and override variables only in F-KEY; the runbook's required headings only in F-RUNBOOK.
F5 depends on G7, because it puts F-CHOICE inside the sweep's spec coherence check.
The fixture overlay is named `story-behind-flag`.
No ledger entry was added: the implementer's existing `test_defects` field carries a test that F-ON names, with its shape unchanged.

fix.summary:
All five findings in the task are decided: four fixed in the design, one left for package F2. (The task text says ten findings; it lists five, and those are the five dealt with.) The four checks are clean and no D31 finding is open or not-fixed in the ledger.

Two findings needed a decision rather than wording.

- **Removal (d31-fix-2-C1-1).** A story now removes a flag in one of two ways, named in `flag_change`: `remove` keeps the new behaviour, `withdraw` gives the feature up. Walking a withdrawal through its red gate showed a defect the finding did not name: nothing can fail first, so the gate could never pass. A withdrawal is now asked for no red test, and its record says so.
- **Moved tests (d31-fix-2-C1-3).** Neither proposed fix worked alone, because an existing test's own name already carries an `ac<N>` from the story that wrote it. A moved test is now evidence of no criterion, and its name has one fixed form so a program can tell which test it was and when it has come back.

For d31-fix-2-C1-4 I did not edit `packaging/build-plan.md`, which is outside this task's write list. I moved the sweep form of F-CHOICE from F5 to F6 instead, so step 5 of the build plan is right as it stands.

Three things to know:

- `rewrite/findings/outcomes/d31-fix-2-2.json` holds a sixth object, for D31R-F-15. Its outcome is unchanged; its text named only `flag_change: remove` and now names both removal values.
- Not changed, outside these findings: the pull request's Rollback and Feature flags sections are written for "a story that names a flag", which includes a removal, where turning the flag off is not a rollback step.
- Not changed, outside these findings: a test can still be moved as `pending` after its flag was turned on; a later `remove` is then the first check to name it.
decisions_made: A story removes a flag in one of two ways, named in flag_change: remove keeps the behaviour of a value other than the default (a release flag's on behaviour); withdraw keeps what the product does with no flag set (the feature is given up).
For a flag that is not boolean, a removal is remove and the story's criteria name the value whose behaviour stays.

A remove is refused at its red gate while the flag still has a pending test, and the message names each; the way through (finish the behaviour behind the flag, or withdraw) is stated in flag-lifecycle.md 'Removal'.
A withdrawal's red gate asks for no red test, applies no red share and maps no test to a criterion, and its record says so, because nothing the product does with no flag set changes.
A withdrawal must bring back every moved test under its own name; it keeps the off and default tests (flag setting and token taken out) rather than deleting them.
After a remove the on tests keep their names; F-DEFINITION refuses any other token of the flag at the head, and after a withdrawal any token at all.
A moved test's name has one fixed form: its own name with __flag_old_<k> or __flag_pending_<k> added, so a program can tell which test it was and when it has come back.
F-STATES checks moved tests exactly instead of by count: a new moved test must be a test of the base report, and a missing test must be held at the head as a moved test.
A moved test, and a test that has come back, is evidence of no criterion and is left out of the criteria map; the move no longer adds the flag-off criterion to the name.
A new off or default test must name a criterion, and only criteria whose text contains 'flag off'.
A split test moves only the part the on state breaks; the rest keeps the name.
The adversary's review-stories checks each flag_change against the request it answers; the item flag-removed covers which tests a removal deletes and that tests brought back or renamed are unchanged.
The sweep form of F-CHOICE is built by F6, not F5; F5 depends on F1 and G5 only, F6 also on F5, and build-plan step 5 stands unedited.
The wider test_defects description is left for F2 under the finding's own id (no new D31-<n> entry), and the story script's prompt is not changed.
F-REMOVE treats any open story that removes the flag, of either kind, as blocking a new cleanup story.
The release packet says, for each flag a release removes, which behaviour stays.
D31R-F-15's open ledger text is re-recorded in the new outcomes file so it names both removal values; its outcome is unchanged.

The design choices hold up and can be enforced, with two exceptions, filed as new minor findings:
- d31-fix-2-C2-1: the split rule conflicts with the adversary's flag-off item. That item asks that a moved test keep its assertions and that no other existing test be weakened, and a correct split breaks both as written.
- d31-fix-2-C2-2: the new criterion refusal uses gate-red's substring match for ac<N>. A name for AC-12 also matches AC-1, and so does a flag key containing 'ac' plus a digit, so a correctly named off test can be refused.

still_open.problem: The test-writer duty now says to split a test: 'Split a test that asserts both kinds: the part the on state breaks is moved, and the rest keeps the name.' The adversary's item flag-off, which is the check for moves, asks that 'each test the diff moves has its assertions unchanged' and that 'the diff deletes, renames or weakens no other existing test'. A correct split fails both as written: the moved part holds only some of the original assertions, and the part that keeps the name has lost them. Nothing checks what a split actually needs, which is that the two parts together keep every assertion of the original, unchanged, even though F-STATES's unmeasured cell hands that question to this item. Also, 'both kinds' comes right after the sentence that defines old and pending, so it can be read as a test that asserts both an old and a pending part.
still_open.proposed_fix: Add to the adversary's item flag-off: for a split test, the moved part and the part that keeps the name together hold every assertion of the original, unchanged, and the moved part holds only what the on state breaks. Exclude the remaining part of a split from 'weakens no other existing test'. In the test-writer duty, write 'Split a test that the on state breaks only in part' instead of 'that asserts both kinds'.

still_open.problem: F-STATES's new refusal rejects a new off or default test whose name 'names one [criterion] whose text lacks the words flag off'. It takes the criteria a name names from gate-red's substring rule ('its name contains ac<N>'). So a test named for AC-12 also names AC-1. The tidy form also allows a key such as 'hvac2-mode', which encodes as 'hvac2_mode', and then the required state token itself names AC-2. In a story with ten or more criteria, or with such a key, an off test named exactly as the duty asks is refused, and the test-writer cannot rename its way out. Before this round the check only asked whether the name named any criterion, so the loose match did no harm.
still_open.proposed_fix: In F-STATES, define which criteria a name names for this refusal: each ac<N> with no letter or digit directly before it and no digit directly after it, read in the name once every token of the flag has been removed. Leave gate-red's own map rule alone, because it is on the thin slice path.
